# Hamburg depot

Hamburg opens at 05:30, the earliest opening time of the depots in the network, and has a cold room holding 25 pallets. Its cold-room capacity is smaller than Rotterdam's 40 pallets. [src: doc:docs/depots.md]

## Cold-chain alarms

At Hamburg a cold-room alarm pages the night manager rather than a shift lead, which matches the site's night-manager staffing model. Every alarm is logged in the incident book within the hour. See [cold-chain alarm response](../procedures/cold-chain-alarm-response.md). [src: doc:docs/alarms.md; doc:docs/staff.md]

The Hamburg alarm rule does not state a temperature threshold or duration, unlike the Rotterdam rule of 8 °C for ten minutes. [src: doc:docs/alarms.md] *(unverified)*

## Staffing

Hamburg's night shift is run by a night manager instead of a shift lead. See [shifts and staffing](../topics/shifts-and-staffing.md). [src: doc:docs/staff.md]

## Safety

Hamburg's most recent documented fire drill found a blocked exit, since cleared. See [depot safety rules](../topics/depot-safety.md). [src: doc:docs/safety.md]

## Connections

Hamburg sits between [Rotterdam depot](rotterdam-depot.md), served by Nordfreight's chilled lane on Tuesdays and Fridays, and [Gdansk depot](gdansk-depot.md), reached by Baltic Reefer's chilled service on Mondays; Van Dijk carries dry goods daily. See [carriers and lanes](../topics/carriers-and-lanes.md). [src: doc:docs/carriers.md]

# Rotterdam depot

Rotterdam is one of the network's chilled-goods depots, open from 06:00 to 22:00. Its cold room holds 40 pallets at 2 to 8 °C, the largest cold storage capacity of the depots described. [src: doc:docs/depots.md]

## Cold storage and alarms

The cold room is the site of the network's documented cold-chain alarm rule: if the room passes 8 °C for ten minutes, the shift lead moves the pallets to a backup room and calls facilities on extension 4410, with the alarm logged in the incident book within the hour. See [cold-chain alarm response](../procedures/cold-chain-alarm-response.md). [src: doc:docs/alarms.md]

The existence of a backup room at Rotterdam is stated in the alarm procedure; the backup room's capacity is not given. [src: doc:docs/alarms.md] *(unverified)*

## Staffing

Rotterdam runs three shifts, each led by a shift lead — the role that owns the cold-room response. See [shifts and staffing](../topics/shifts-and-staffing.md). [src: doc:docs/staff.md]

## Connections

Rotterdam is one end of Nordfreight's chilled lane to [Hamburg depot](hamburg-depot.md); Van Dijk carries dry goods daily to the depot. Each carrier presents a temperature log at hand-over. See [carriers and lanes](../topics/carriers-and-lanes.md). [src: doc:docs/carriers.md]

Returns are inspected at the depot that shipped them, so Rotterdam handles its own outbound returns. See [returns handling](../topics/returns-handling.md). [src: doc:docs/returns.md]

# Antwerp depot

Antwerp opens at 07:00, the latest opening time of the depots in the network, and has no cold room. Because of that it cannot hold chilled goods in refrigerated storage. [src: doc:docs/depots.md]

## Staffing

Antwerp runs two shifts. The documents do not name a shift-lead count for the site, though each Rotterdam shift has a shift lead and six pickers. See [shifts and staffing](../topics/shifts-and-staffing.md). [src: doc:docs/staff.md] *(unverified)*

## Returns

Antwerp accepts its own returns for inspection, since returns are always inspected at the depot that shipped them and never at another depot. See [returns handling](../topics/returns-handling.md). [src: doc:docs/returns.md]

With no cold room, the chilled-returns window (arrival within 24 hours of dispatch, otherwise destruction) has no documented on-site refrigerated staging point at Antwerp. [src: doc:docs/depots.md; doc:docs/returns.md] *(unverified)*

# Returns handling

Returns are governed by a product-type deadline and a fixed inspection location. [src: doc:docs/returns.md]

## Deadlines

- **Chilled returns** must arrive within 24 hours of dispatch; otherwise they are destroyed. [src: doc:docs/returns.md]
- **Dry returns** are accepted for 30 days. [src: doc:docs/returns.md]

## Inspection location

A return is inspected at the depot that shipped it, never at another depot. This means each depot carries the inspection workload for its own outbound volume rather than routing returns to the nearest site. [src: doc:docs/returns.md]

## Cold-room dependency

Only Rotterdam and Hamburg have cold rooms (40 and 25 pallets respectively); Antwerp has none and Gdansk handles dry goods only. The 24-hour chilled window therefore lands on the two depots with refrigerated storage. [src: doc:docs/depots.md]

The documents do not state whether the 24-hour clock runs from carrier hand-over or from leaving the customer, nor how a chilled return is held if it arrives outside depot hours. [src: doc:docs/returns.md] *(unverified)*

Related: [carriers and lanes](carriers-and-lanes.md) (temperature logs at hand-over), [Rotterdam depot](../entities/rotterdam-depot.md), [Antwerp depot](../entities/antwerp-depot.md).

# Cold-chain alarm response

The cold-chain alarm procedure covers a cold room drifting above its chilled range. It is documented for [Rotterdam depot](../entities/rotterdam-depot.md) and, differently, for [Hamburg depot](../entities/hamburg-depot.md). [src: doc:docs/alarms.md]

## Trigger and actions at Rotterdam

- **Trigger:** the Rotterdam cold room passes 8 °C for ten minutes. [src: doc:docs/alarms.md]
- **Relocation:** the shift lead moves the pallets to the backup room. [src: doc:docs/alarms.md]
- **Escalation:** the shift lead calls facilities on extension 4410. [src: doc:docs/alarms.md]

The 8 °C trigger sits at the top of the room's stated 2 to 8 °C holding range, and the room's capacity is 40 pallets. [src: doc:docs/depots.md] The capacity of the backup room is not documented. [src: doc:docs/alarms.md] *(unverified)*

## Actions at Hamburg

At Hamburg the alarm pages the night manager rather than a shift lead, consistent with the night-manager night shift at that site. The documents do not give a Hamburg threshold or a physical response step. See [shifts and staffing](../topics/shifts-and-staffing.md). [src: doc:docs/alarms.md; doc:docs/staff.md] *(unverified)*

## Logging

Every alarm, at any depot, is logged in the incident book within the hour. [src: doc:docs/alarms.md]

## Not covered by the sources

The documents describe no cold room at Antwerp or Gdansk, and so no alarm path for those sites. [src: doc:docs/depots.md] *(unverified)*
", "path": "wiki/procedures/cold-chain-alarm-response.md"}

append.description: append to the report instead of replacing it

path.description: report path relative to the reports/ output folder
